# B-Rar

> B-Rar (also written BRar) is a free (for personal and non-commercial use) archive extractor for Windows 10 and 11 and for Macs with Apple Silicon (macOS 13 or later), written in Rust. It extracts ZIP, RAR, 7z and tar archives in parallel on all CPU cores, faster than WinRAR and 7-Zip, makes ZIP archives on all cores (with optional AES-256 passwords), and adds a Windows 11 right-click menu (Open in B-Rar, Extract files, Extract to folder, Extract here, Test archive, Add to archive, Add to "name.zip").

- Mac: `brew install --cask ahmedanjum30/tap/b-rar` (Homebrew tap: https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/homebrew-tap): a native app (archive browser, Finder Quick Actions: Extract Here, Extract to Folder, Extract Files, Open in B-Rar, Test Archive, Add to ZIP, Add to Archive) and the `brar` command line. Or B-Rar-<version>-macos.zip from the latest release. On an M3 Pro it extracts ZIPs about 4x faster than Archive Utility with many small files (70,000 files: 3.0 s against 13.2 s) and 1.3x with large ones (4 GB: 5.4 s against 6.9 s). Against macOS's command-line extractors (3.4 GB ZIP, 20,008 files, M3 Pro): B-Rar 2.3 s, bsdtar 10.4 s, ditto 11.0 s, unzip 22.7 s.
- Linux: the command line only, `brar`, in B-Rar-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz from https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Rar/releases/latest (x86-64, glibc 2.39+).
- Install: the installer at https://ahmedanjum30.github.io/B-Rar/download/B-Rar-Setup.exe, or the portable zip from https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Rar/releases/latest. Microsoft Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9MZKQXC7PFCH (or `winget install 9MZKQXC7PFCH`).
- Source code and documentation: https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Rar
- Benchmarks: https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Rar/blob/main/benches/RESULTS.md
- License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (free for personal, non-commercial, educational and public use; commercial use not permitted)
- Author: Ahmad Anjum (https://github.com/ahmedanjum30)

## Features

- Formats: ZIP (Deflate, Deflate64, BZip2, LZMA, XZ, Zstandard, PPMd, AES, ZipCrypto), RAR 4 and 5 (solid, encrypted, multi-volume), 7z, tar, tar.gz, tar.xz, tar.zst, tar.bz2, single .gz/.xz/.zst/.bz2 files.
- Speed (1.1 GB RAR5 archive, all cores): B-Rar 2.0 s, WinRAR 4.0 s, 7-Zip 8.1 s, Windows tar 15.1 s. Archives with ~48,000 small files: B-Rar 7.1 s, 7-Zip 24.2 s, WinRAR 28.2 s. 7z (LZMA2) archives are still faster with 7-Zip.
- Archive browser: look inside an archive, search it, open single files, extract only selected files and folders.
- Archives in parts: RAR volumes (.part1.rar, .r00) and split archives (.001); extraction can start from any part.
- Passwords, including encrypted file names. Asks before replacing files. Extracting into admin-only folders shows the Windows UAC prompt.
- Command line: `B-Rar x archive.rar`, `B-Rar l`, `B-Rar t`.
- Creates ZIP archives only (not RAR or 7z): `B-Rar a backup.zip folder`, or Add to archive / Add to "name.zip" in the right-click menu.
- Alternative to: WinRAR, 7-Zip, PeaZip, Bandizip, the Windows built-in ZIP and tar support.

## Privacy

B-Rar collects no data; it only asks GitHub whether a newer version is out (the Microsoft Store version doesn't connect at all): https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Rar/blob/main/PRIVACY.md
